utterances.text: But this softer line was there for a short period of time it seems. What is your assessment? Do you know what he was in charge of as deputy federal prime minister?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was in charge of international cooperation as deputy federal prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Last question, and I'll stop torturing you. Mr. Stamp will continue. What is your assess many of the political decisions held by Mr. Sainovic, his political views?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period in which we cooperated most directly, I knew Mr. Sainovic to be a man of dialogue, prepared to listen to arguments and accept them, a tolerant person, and prepared to build compromise and skilful at bringing compromise, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would conclude my examination-in-chief. Your witness, Counsellor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does any Defence counsel wish to cross-examine? Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jovanovic. Do you know any other senior member of the SPS by the name Milan Jovanovic, who shares your name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last document you were shown is 2D25. That's tab what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should be tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tab 1. And you see a list a list of the persons who are present at the session of the party. Among them, just around the middle of the list, you'll see one Mihalj Kertes. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He was in charge of the customs organisation in Serbia at the time, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did he or did he not hand over to you any money from custom revenues in cash?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did he deliver to you any money at all in cash?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He handed over to me some money in cash for financing the Socialist Party of Serbia, but not customs money but money that he had collected from different donors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How much?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was seven years ago. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Give us an approximation, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two million marks at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was this one delivery or more than one delivery?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me about something that happened seven years ago. I do not remember, and I don't see why that matters for proceedings like these, when Mihalj Kertes will be tried before a court in Serbia as of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, it's not for you to decide what questions should or should not be answered in this court. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did you receive this money, in one transaction or more than one transaction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You mean you don't remember if you received two million marks in cash on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So was it one occasion or more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall on how many occasions I received it. Was it one occasion or was it more than one? I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I understand that answer.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you saying that you might have received two million marks in cash on one single occasion, but you don't recall whether you did?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say to you that I do not remember whether I got it on one occasion or on several occasions the amount that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Can you recall, approximately, when you got the amount?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, was it in 1999, 1998, 1997, 2000? Do you remember the year?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In what capacity did you receive this money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As secretary of the Technical Services of the Main Board of the SPS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You referred to 2D384, a document that we don't have translations for, but I'm just going off your description of what this agreement meant. You were asked a question by Judge Bonomy. I just want to get what you're saying is clear. You're saying that this agreement meant that parties to civil suits could choose the ethnicity of the tribunal that they would bring the suit before? Is that what is written in the document? May I ask you that question first? Is that what is written in the document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that's tab 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In that regard, you were previously directed to Article V, 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for it to be precise, I'm going to read out to you paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: We do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Citizens and legal persons in Kosovo will be ensured the right to select the court that will try them. Every citizen and legal person in Kosmet, at the beginning of court proceedings, civil, non-contentious, and criminal, as the prosecutor, the proposer, or the accused may choose whether he will be tried by the court of the Republic of Serbia or the Kosmet court."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, are you saying that this was something that was agreed upon sincerely as a policy that could work in Kosovo where there were ethnic tensions? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. Had this not been sincere, it would not have been proposed; and had they seen it in a different light, the representatives of ethnic communities comprising almost half of the population in Kosovo would not have signed it. The problem of Kosmet arose because such institutions had not been put in place, institutions that would ensure full national equality. I firmly believe that, had there been a chance for such institutions to be established, they would have been successful. I'm not saying that there would have been no problems and difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was going to get to this later, but before I forget let me ask you this, and this question is in the context of what you just said: "Representatives of ethnic communities comprising almost half of the population would have signed it." What was the population of Kosovo at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact figures; but according to the census, those who declared themselves as Albanians represented the dominant group. However, I know for a fact that there were more than 350.000 Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you're saying that representatives comprising almost half of the population would not have signed it. What proportion of the population did those representatives amount to? What do you mean by "almost half"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to 47, 48 per cent of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This would be the non-Albanian population in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I also believe that this paper, had a proper chance been given, would also have been supported by at least one-third of the Albanians, and that would constitute a good majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. But let us just focus on those that you referred to that signed it; 47 to 48 per cent of the population, you said, and that would be the non-Albanian population of Kosovo. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely that: Serbs, Montenegrins, Muslims, Turks, Egyptians, Roma; that is to say, ethnic communities which existed and functioning in Kosmet. It wasn't just Albanians living in Kosmet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like there to be no speculation. Are there any signatures of Albanians there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. Sokol Cuse, democratic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is not proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, you'll get a chance to re-examine. That was an inappropriate interruption. It is not for you to ask questions at this stage. You can clarify later. Please continue, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say 40 per cent -- 47, 48 per cent of the population of Kosovo who were non-Albanian, is that your personal position or was it the position of your party?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a statistical fact. As for the status and the rights of ethnic communities, it is well known that it is not just a matter of figures. Regardless of how many members of an ethnic group there are in any particular state, each state is duty-bound to ensure that their rights are guaranteed and implemented, regardless of their numbers, in order to prevent assimilation, in order for them to preserve their national identity. This is something that has been proclaimed by --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We'll get to that, but I asked a simple question. Do you recall the question I asked you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The answer was that it was a statistical fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, is this a statistical fact that is accepted by you personally, or was this statistical fact, as you call it, the position accepted by your party, that 47 to 48 per cent of the Kosovo Albanian population -- of the population in Kosovo were not Albanian? That is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was that the position of your party?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Nor do I. You must know the Serbian approach to things in general by now well enough, Mr. Stamp, to know that if it's a statistical fact then they accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is, the party accepts it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not a matter of opinion. It's a fact according to the witness. Let's move on. This is not producing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm prepared to accept the Court's position as a whole that the cross-examination should proceed, but I would just like to know before I proceed if I can accept that his answer is that the party that he has been speaking about, that he's a member of, accepts this as a statistical fact, if that is what his answer means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you may ask him again if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one time, Mr. Jovanovic. Did the SPS accept as a statistical that 48 per cent or 47 percent of the people who lived in Kosovo were not Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly don't know how to answer that question. You're asking me to tell you that the party assembled a meeting and said, "We support the Republican Bureau for Statistics, which in 1991 carried out a census saying there were so many Serbs, so many Albanians, and so on. No political party does this. However, I have full confidence in official organs. It would be the same as asking: Do you believe today is the 22nd of August. I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is your answer, giving these figures, based on a census in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially on the basis of the census and partially based on some other facts. When I told you about the number of Serbs, I can also tell you that today in Serbia the international organisations have about 235.000 citizens registered who had been displaced from Kosovo after NATO aggression. Also, pursuant to the records of international organisations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, just concentrate on the question I've asked you. It's a very simple question, and you say now that it's partially based on that census and partially based on some other facts. Now, is your impression or understanding that that census was carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So there are figures available from that census telling us how many Albanians there are in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and those figures are available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In 1D114, that's tab -- the last tab, I think. Tab 11. You will see that the representatives of the non-Albanian community in that letter gave their number as 600.000.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to tell me which tab this is so I could take a look?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is tab 11, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it. Yes, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And, in that letter, they represented their number to be 600.000.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise, they say over 600.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. Did you -- were you aware of a report by Helge Brunborg of the 14th of August, 2002, in respect to the ethnic composition of the population of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. If you look at D114 and look at the signatories of D114, can you tell me how many of those persons who signed that document were not members of either the TEC or the Socialist Party?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you understand the question? You are saying that there were seven persons that signed who were not members of either TEC or the Socialist Party?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please explain this acronym "TEC"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The acronym is for the Provisional Executive Council for Kosovo and Metohija that was headed by Mr. Zoran Andjelkovic that you spoke about. So I'll ask again. How many persons there do you know had who have signed this document who are not members of that board or the Socialist Party? If you don't know, you can say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the figures for the provisional Executive Council. As for the Socialist Party of Serbia, I already gave you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. Well, let's look at it. Sokol Cuse. Do you know if he was a member of the TEC or the Provisional Executive Council?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the composition of the Provisional Executive Council, so I cannot give an answer to that portion of that question. I don't know who comprised that counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. So, therefore, you're not able to say whether Faik Jashari, Zeynelabidin Kyreys, Guljbehar Sabovic, Ibro Vait, Ljuan Koka, Cerim Abazi were members of the TEC, would you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That questions been answered, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I'm press on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The members of the TEC were appointed by Zoran Andjelkovic. Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I think that the composition of the Provisional Executive Council was up to some other organ. Some other organ appointed them. I don't think that it was only within the competence of the president. However, I'm not certain, and I cannot answer that question with full certainty. If he did that, then he probably was authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Similarly, Mr. Jovanovic, I suggest to you that the signatories in 2D384, at least seven of the ten signatories - and that is the agreement for self-government of Kosovo of the 15th of March, which gave persons the right to choose their own judges or judges from their own ethnicity - seven of the ten persons who signed this document were either members of the TEC or the SPS. I represent that to you; do you agree or do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that statement. This was a state delegation, and party affiliation is not important at all. It was the Assembly and the government who approved them, and the fact that they were members of some political parties should not constitute a problem in my mind. The Socialist Party of Serbia was the most prominent one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, that's not the point that's being put to you. It would appear that you do not know the answer to the question, and the question is whether seven of the ten persons who signed the document were either members of the Executive Council or of the SPS. And we all know people can have two positions. They can be one thing in respect of one matter, and they can be a party member in respect of another matter. So is your answer, again, that you don't know, or can you clarify this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have just put two questions to me. I don't know which of these people who signed the agreement were also on the Provisional Executive Council, but I know for a fact that seven of them were not members of the SPS, or at least not all seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Seven were not members of the SPS; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who presented this document to the Kosovo Albanians in Paris?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you're well aware, the discussions in Paris were organised in such a way that the delegations never met directly; that is to say, that our document was submitted via the negotiating troika.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, we are past the time for a break. Can you find a suitable time to interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Jovanovic, we have to have another break at this stage. Would you again please go with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we will resume at five to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, do you have any examples of this, and do you want to tender them in writing before we finish today and just give a list of examples, the page references, to the clerk?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have decided to do exactly that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it has to be today before we finish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They will type it up now, and you will have it in five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When we left off, you were saying, Mr. Jovanovic, that the document, this agreement, was submitted to the Kosovo Albanians via the negotiating troika. Now, the negotiating troika would be the ambassadors of the Contact Group?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So they were given this document in Paris on the 15th of March or thereabouts, and asked to ask the Albanian delegation to sign it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was offered prior to this date to the Albanian delegation, several days prior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I attended the talks held by our delegation in Paris.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question is: How do you know the document was handed to the Albanian delegation? It's a simple question. Are you assuming it, or do you know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, I was there with the delegation during the negotiations in Paris, and I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But your evidence, so far, is that it was handed to the negotiators, not directly by your delegation to the Albanian delegation. Are you now saying it was handed directly by your delegation to the Albanian delegation? Because we understood they never met each other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you're quite right. We submitted this document to the negotiating troika, and we were sure that they handed it over to the Albanian delegation. We were there to negotiate, and we thought that the same applied, just as they provided documents to our delegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you assume the document was handed to the Albanian delegation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not assuming. There's no reason for me to doubt that the negotiators did not give the document to the Albanian delegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what is your positive basis for saying that they did actually give it to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The main role of the negotiators was to pass the proposals from one side to the other. If they gave us the proposals of the Albanian side, then I think it was quite reasonable to believe that they also passed our proposals to the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may move to a different area, sir. You said, in discussing some of these minutes of Executive Council meetings, that there were occasions or there was a situation sometime in the autumn of 1998 where Kosovo Albanians were handing in arms. That's correct? You said that; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, these weren't meetings of the Executive Council, but meetings of the Main Board. I think it was in September. If you can give me the tab number, sir, I think the meeting you're referring to was on the 27th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's recorded, I think, in tab 3 on the 22nd of September as an Executive Board meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. This is the meeting that took place on the 22nd, and it is the Executive Board and not the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was it ever discussed at any SPS meeting, in your presence, that the Kosovo Albanian population should be disarmed? I'm not talking about persons who might have been members of the KLA or any other, what you describe as, separatist organisation, but the population in general should be disarmed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember specifically any discussions from the Main and Executive Boards. There was quite a large number of meetings. Essentially, whatever was discussed was recorded in the conclusions; therefore, I can't be more specific than this in answer to your question, and I certainly do not wish to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know of discussions within any of those organs of the party, among senior members of the party, in regard to the idea that Serbs in Kosovo should be armed; that is, Serb civilians in Kosovo should be armed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any direct information that would allow me to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand that answer. It was an answer -- a question that required a yes or no answer. Do you know of any discussions about arming the Serb civilians in Kosovo, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you attended all the Main Board meetings and all the Executive Board meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And persons, for example, Vojislav Zivkovic, also attended these Main Board meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was his role and function in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the president of the Provincial Board of the SPS; I mean, for Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In other words, he was the president of the board for the party in that very pressing and dominant issue that the party was facing in this period of time. Can I ask you this: Do you know not know whether or not he raised the issue of arming Serbs in Kosovo? Was that issue ever raised by him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at Exhibit P2828. Could we go to page 2. Can you see, sir, that this is a letter from Mr. Zivkovic, dated 19 June, 1998, to President Milutinovic? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The image on the screen is poor. Could I have a hard copy of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at the top of the document, you can see it's dated the 19th of June, 1998, and it's addressed to President Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of the document, the foot of the document, you'll see that it's signed by president of the Provincial Board of the SPS of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sealed also.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It says, in the last paragraph, that: "Able-bodied Serbs in Kosovo and Metohija should be organised into formations, armed, and used to defend and protect our country in the area." I think that's "our country in the area." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you -- having seen that, would -- do you recall whether or not there was this discussion amongst senior members of the SPS in any forum; that is, the arming of Serbs in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I set eyes on this letter. At the meetings of the Main and Executive Boards of the Socialist Party of Serbia or any other of its working bodies - and I mean any of the meetings that I attended - there were no ideas, requests, or proposals to arm the local Serbs; quite the contrary, in fact. The party line was clear. Sovereignty was what was at stake in Kosovo, and sovereignty could not be defended individually or through some sort of a private war; rather, the defence of territorial integrity and sovereignty should be left to bodies whose job it is to do just that, the police and the army. If I may, just to add something. I do not challenge the authenticity of this letter. However, if you look at the previous positions, you see that the direct reason for this letter was the murder of a 70-year-old elderly person who was brutally taken off a bus and shot. There were probably a lot of heated passions. There was probably a lot of stuff being said that was too heated, and there were incidents occurring that led to this. However, if I talk about the official meetings of the boards which I attended, there was no mention of the Serbs being armed, and there were no hints, indeed, that the Serbs should be armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It stands to reason, then, that it is possible, indeed likely, that these discussions could have occurred between senior members of the party outside of those meetings that you attended, those official party meetings.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase your question in a clearer way, because I'm not here to answer any assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: All right. I'll ask another question. Do you know whether on the ground in Kosovo, in 1999, armed Serbs who were not members of the security forces were used in operations by the security forces? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no direct information about military operations in Kosmet; therefore, I'm unable to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would it surprise you if that was the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have a position on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I find that a little strange, in view of what you said a moment ago about the party's position: "It was clear that sovereignty could not be defended with private armies and the matter should be left to bodies whose job it is to do just that, the police and the army." So you wouldn't be surprised if the army arranged for the arming -- or used the civilian Serb population, duly armed, in operations in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply cannot say whether I'd be surprised or not based on an assumption alone. I simply have no facts indicating anything about that; therefore, I believe that the state organs acted in keeping with the military regulations that applied at the time. I can't just take an assumption and express a surprise or indeed reservations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand that answer. That's precisely what it is appropriate to invite you to do in relation to speculation, express whether it would be a surprise to you or not. If, as a matter of fact, it were proved in this court that Serb civilians were used in this way, you must know whether that would surprise you or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this were an official fact backed by evidence, that could indicate my surprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The group of three that was delegated to go to Kosovo, that is, Mr. Andjelkovic, Mr. Matkovic, and Mr. Minic, when were they disbanded, or should I ask, were they officially disbanded?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember an official decision to disband that group; however, I do know that, as early as late September, they reduced the amount of their activities. After attending a session of the Provincial Board of the SPS in late October, their activity, as team, practically ceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, if you look at D88 - and I think that's tab 5 - that's a meeting of the 28th of October. And you'll see immediately before III - that's on the third page in English, but if you look for the III on your copy - that even on the 28th of April [sic], they were still functioning and were still mandated to do work and submit reports thereafter. What I want to ask you is: Having read to that, do you -- have you seen any document at all dealing with the disbanding of this group?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mention April. At tab 5, I see the 27th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: October, right. I really meant October, because you had said that they stopped working in October, and that is why I'm asking you. You were saying they stopped working in October, and we see here, on the 28th of October, they were obviously working, and they had been tasked to do other work. So, having regard to that, which is on the document, can you say whether or not you have seen any document which terminated this group, this executive group?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not the established practice in the Socialist Party of Serbia to adopt official documents on determination of any group. Quite simply, their activity ceases as soon as the reasons for which it is originally established are no longer there. If you look at item (B) of the minutes dated the 27th of October, 1998, what we see there is that they would attend the next meeting of the Provincial Board, which was due to be held in a matter of days; therefore, they attended that meeting, and that was when their activity ceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us about the organisation of the government in 1998, that there was a coalition, and who were the members of that coalition in the latter part of 1998 and the beginning of 1999? Which parties?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coalition in the Republic of Serbia was made up of the following parties: The Socialist Party of Serbia, the Serbian Radical Party, and the Yugoslav Left. As for the federal level, as for the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the People's Socialist Party of Montenegro was involved, and later also the Serbian Renewal Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Among those groups that you mention, would it be correct to say that the two strongest elements of that coalition would be the Socialist Party and the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In coalition governments, there is no stronger or weaker partner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Go ahead, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to say is this: Sometimes a minor party or the lesser partner, in a manner of speaking, can have more pull in the government because its potential to blackmail the other party might be greater; however, it is true that the SPS and the Serb Radical Party, in terms of the numbers of their delegates, were the majority parties, the two major parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, before we talk about that, let me ask you another question in reference to 1D443. And that is a political -- that is at tab 10. You don't need to look at it. I'm just reminding you what it is. It's a political -- that's a gazette of Serbia of the 4th of February, 1999, a political platform for mandate for delegates of the Republic of Serbia. It was adopted by the Federal Assembly or by the Republican Assembly; which one is it? Remind me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It says clearly it's the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what were the parties involved in adopting that mandate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for these conclusions, we enjoyed the support, not just of the Socialist Party of Serbia but also of the Serbian Radical Party and the Yugoslav Left and the Serbian Renewal Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were they the only parties in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did the other parties in the Assembly also endorse that mandate, as you call it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. I think that the democratic party was the only one not to lend their support. That's as far as I remember about the democratic party, and I can't speak about any other parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Serbian Radical Party was headed by whom?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you aware that for -- let me put it this way: Are you aware that Mr. Seselj had proposed the expulsion of some Albanians from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are not aware, I take it, that Mr. Seselj had for many years claimed that hundreds of thousands of Albanians had crossed into Kosovo, and that they were not truly members of the population of Kosovo and, therefore, they should be expelled? You are not aware that the leader of the party that was in partnership with you propounded that policy?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What matters in coalitions is what is translated into official state documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor put two questions to me. Could he repeat them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you not aware that Mr. Seselj claimed that there were hundreds of thousands of Albanians living in Kosovo who were not from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that claim, and that is a true fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware that he proposed that they should be expelled from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are a political scientist, so I'll ask you this question: Are you aware of a political movement in Kosovo, in Serbia, that sought to understate the number of Albanians that lived in Kosovo? Did you know that many political leaders and intellectuals in Serbia sought to understate the number of Albanians that live in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask you that you put questions to me one by one, but I am going to answer these simultaneously. This is the first time I of the existence of some kind of movement; or to put it more specifically, there was no such movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Let's talk about yourself, then. You, sir, today, in answer to questions from the President of this Panel, said that 47 to 48 per cent of the population of Kosovo that were not Albanians. You said that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And twice, in answer to his question, said it was a statistical fact based on the 1991 census. You recall saying that? Twice.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, I said, in the census of 1991 and other censuses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But when you were asked after that about precisely what you meant, and it is a matter of the record, you agreed that you're basing the statistical fact on the census of 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, but it also has to do with the other facts that I talked about, the number of refugees and displaced persons from Kosmet living in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which is what I was about to ask you about. Remember, we are speaking about 1999, March, the early part of 1999, before the NATO intervention. What are the other factors, apart from the 1991 census, that you base this estimate of the proportion of non-Albanians and Albanians in Kosovo on? What are the other factors?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the census in 1991, from then until the other date, ten years elapsed. Fluctuations of the population in Kosovo and Metohija were very pronounced throughout that period of time. A large number of Albanians came from Macedonia and went to Macedonia and other places. So that structure that was established by the consensus and that we can simply get from any web site of the republic -- republican statistics office, for instance, that structure was changed. In the letter of the ethnic communities, you saw that they claimed that there were more than 600.000 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let me get back to the question, and I'll ask it a different way. I'll ask you the question. You twice told His Honour that you were basing your estimate on the 1991 census. You also say other factors. I'm asking you what are the other factors that you base your numbers on?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, population movements: People moving in, people moving abroad. After all, there were many articles in newspapers and in professional periodicals that refer to changed structures in Kosovo and Metohija. Will you allow me just one more sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sure, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For seven years, the international community has been in Kosovo and Metohija. Can we get official data from the international community regarding the situation in Kosovo and Metohija? No, we cannot. A census was not carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you. You are saying, sir, I take it from what you're saying -- all right. Let me just ask this. Are you saying that you don't rely on the 1991 census? I understood you to be saying twice that you relied on the 1991 census to make your estimation, and now it seems as if you're saying that events following 1991 that were reported in the press cause you to change. Are you relying on the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not relying on it fully. I am not only relying on what the press wrote about this, but also the writing of professional periodicals. I am not denying the fact that the Albanians constituted a majority of the population in Kosovo if. That is the point of your question. I'm just trying to say that the members of other ethnic communities constituted a significant group, not a small group in Kosovo and Metohija. I assume that you certainly have the census from 1991, and perhaps you could tell us, so that we don't use this much time for this subject which is quite accessible to all because there is a proper statistics census from 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is P1960, and I don't know if it needs to be raised in e-court. I'm going to refer to page 8. I'm sure my learned friend on the other side are aware of -- sorry, page 9. I think, it's page 8 in the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The 1991 census was boycotted by the majority of the Kosovo Albanian population. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask that I be presented the document in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the document as yet, sir. I'm asking you if you know whether or not the 1991 population census was boycotted by the majority of the Kosovo Albanian population. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I represent to you that the census was nonetheless conducted by the federal statistical office and they made a statistical estimate, and they found that the total population of Kosovo in 1991 was 1.96 million, of which 9.9 per cent were Serbs and 8.5 per cent were in the category other, while 81.6 per cent were Albanians. Do you dispute that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These data of the statistics office are problematic for several reasons, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, before we speak about the problem, sir, I'll be thankful if you'll just answer my question. Do you dispute that these were the findings of the federal statistics office of the government?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't received this document. I would like you to show it to me in the Serbian language and a hard copy if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we get to the document, I remind you, sir, that you told the Court twice that your assessment was based on the 1991 census, and that is your assessment as to the relative proportion of various ethnicities living in Kosovo. Do you know not know that the federal statistics office estimate in the 1991 census was that 81.6 per cent of the population in Kosovo were Albanians? Do you dispute that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN JOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A large number of citizens who declared themselves as Albanians were actually members of other ethnic communities who could not freely state their --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Stop there. Just answer this question, please: Are you aware that these were the findings of the federal statistics office? You'll get your chance to say what you want in due course. Let's get over this hurdle first of all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask to be shown that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're being asked on the basis of your own personal recollection. Did you know that these were the findings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I do not know that the federal statistics office estimated; that is to say, that it wasn't a matter of registering, but of estimating such a number of Albanians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, do you wish to continue with this at this stage to complete the point, or do you wish to interrupt? It's a matter for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just ask a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, having regard to the answers I've been getting, it's probably pointless. We could perhaps proceed tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Jovanovic, we have to vacate this courtroom now because another case sits here in the afternoon. We shall have to resume your evidence tomorrow morning at 9.00. It's very important - I can't stress how important - that between now and then, you have absolutely no discussion whatsoever with anyone at all about the evidence in this case. You can talk to whomsoever you wish about whatever you wish as long as there is absolutely no discussion of the evidence. So please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you tomorrow again at 9.00.
